description: I'm not very aware of the bibliometric tools in python and really not up on the topic in general.  ---------- Forwarded message --------- From:   Gregory Leazer  < leazer@g.ucla.edu > Date: Mon, Mar 23, 2020 at 8:54 PM Subject: Re: R and bibliometrics To: Tim Dennis < tdennis@library.ucla.edu > I still haven't quite found the tools I want to use with R...  Might there be better setups if I used Python? On Wed, Mar 18, 2020 at 4:08 PM Gregory Leazer < leazer@g.ucla.edu > wrote: This is great, thank you so much!  I hope you are holding up well. This is a class on bibliometrics, first and foremost, but I would also love it if it fit with additional professional needs.  Beyond R, or instead of it, are there resources that you would recommend? As for R itself, the Data Carpentry tools are pretty light and raw.  Do you have suggestions for other online (doh!) resources for R?   Thanks, and I am sure to have more questions in the coming days, --Greg Leazer On Mon, Feb 3, 2020 at 10:04 AM Tim Dennis < tdennis@library.ucla.edu > wrote: Greg, Sounds like a fun class.  For folks I hire into the lab I look more for general data skills and some scripting language. If they are aware of current practices in R or Python, like the tidyverse in R or pandas and ML frameworks in Python, that’s a bonus. Bibliometrix sounds right, but I don’t do a bunch of bibliometrics stuff (we don’t get researchers coming in with those cases a bunch). However, regarding data, I have a friend at UMN that put up these resources:  https://libguides.umn.edu/c.php?g=895901&p=6443620#s-lg-box-wrapper-24020356 Also, check out some of the ROpenSci  https://ropensci.org/  packages, they have an Altmetric package < https://docs.ropensci.org/rAltmetric/ >, rentrez (pubmed) < https://docs.ropensci.org/rentrez/ > and other packages designed to aid with acquiring data.  Lastly, we do have access to the web of science API. You could generate a bib dB with that for the class. Email  jchan3@library.ucla.edu  for access to that.  Good luck with the class and don’t hesitate to send your students to us for R help. summary: Choosing the Right Statistical Test
description: Hi there! I am doing policy research and am trying to analyze representation of community engagement across gender (male and female) and ethnicity (Hispanic and non-Hispanic). For my research, I am comparing percentages of survey respondents who engaged in different types of community engagement (types organized on 1-5 scale). For example, for gender, I split up my respondents into male and female respondents and calculated percentages of respondents who engaged in different modes of community engagement. I did the same thing for ethnicity. I was hoping to utilize a statistical test in order to draw more precise conclusions about whether or not the differences between percentages of engagement across demographics is statistically significant. However, I am not sure what statistical test I should use to analyze this. I believe my independent variable would be binary and my dependent variable would be categorical ordinal. Hopefully that helps. Any advice that you have on statistical tests would be great! Also, if you have any recommendations for doing these statistical analyses in R Studio, that would also be helpful!

description: From:  Stevens, Marissa <stevensma@humnet.ucla.edu> Sent:  Monday, June 22, 2020 2:13 PM To:  Daniels, Doug <dougdaniels@library.ucla.edu> Subject:  FW: FW: Getting Your Advice on a Potential Project       Dear Doug,   I’m writing to ask for your advice on a potential project the Pourdavoud Center for the Study of the Iranian World is going to undertake.  Apologies if I have reached out to the wrong person – I have been directed to reach out to the Data Science Center, so I thought that I might start with you as a point of contact to see if you can provide me with some advice and guidance on the following project:  There is a collection of seals and seal impressions from Persepolis, and we would like to transfer ownership of the database of photos, drawings, text files, etc. of this collection to UCLA.  It is currently a bit scattered, with some of the files being held by a professor at Trinity University in Texas, and some of the files held in OCHRE at the OI at the University of Chicago.  Below are excerpts from email from Professor Mark Garrison of Trinity University, where he explains the collection and expresses his wishes of what can be accomplished (namely a searchable database and secure storage of all the files).     So, first you will know that the OI has a lot of material on their very difficult platform called OCHRE. It is almost impenetrable and basically worthless as a research device owing to its complexity and slow speed. Rather amazingly, despite its intricacies, no one, not even we editors, can do a basic search on it. Making any changes to it globally, i.e, doing a very basic FIND and the REPLACE is not possible. OCHRE was developed primarily as a vehicle for studying the texts, and it has some amazingly sophisticated tools, if you have the time to learn how to use them.   In any case, as I mentioned, I have talked to Matt Stopler and he knows about our plan to establish a research vehicle for the seals and he is in agreement. I am thinking of something very straight forward that does not require an elaborate IT infrastructure. Because of the nature of our work and the fact that we are still processing seal impressions, it must be flexible enough to allow for changes by the editors (myself and whoever else we so designate). The most common types of changes are:   1) collation of seal numbers (i.e., when we recognize that what we though were two seals in fact are one; as an example, say we realize that PFATS 559 is in fact PFUTS 201; the number PFATS 559 is removed and all information linked with it now goes to PFUTS 201);   2) changing the thematic category of a seal (often happens when we find new impressions of a seal giving us new information about the design);   3) modifying or adding to the list of thematic categories (e.g., we process a new seal and the design requires the creation of a new thematic category; this in fact is very rare at this point).   What I think of as the “fields” in the database (I use a standard flat-file database, File Maker Pro) would be    seal number: e.g., PFS 1*   tablet numbers on which a seal occurs: e.g, PF 45, PFAT 800, PFUT 345, etc.   primary thematic category: e.g., I.a.5. Hero controls winged lion creatures secondary thematic category (rare): e.g., XXII.k. Heraldic: Winged human-faced/human-headed lions references to places where the image has been published: e.g., Garrison 2017, pp. xx-xx, plate xx.   OIP catalogue number (where relevant): e.g., Cat.No. 45 Iconographic key words: e.g., winged symbol, Persian court robe, etc.   The seal number is the key field for organizational purposes.   We would want, of course, to have with each seal number the:   collated line drawing   a sample of photographs of impressions of the seal   Users will want to search the database for specific values in each of these fields and get a list of results with access to the full record with images.   All the data that I have just described are in various File Maker tables.   The images are tiff or jpg format.   Currently, there are 4053 seals that have legible designs. We have 752 seals that we classify as analytically illegible.   Drawings: all 4053 legible seals have been drawn, but those drawings vary from finished (measured) publication-quality drawings to sketches. The sketches are for the most part pretty good and usable, but there are about 50-100 (out of 4053) that need to be replaced because they are not very good. So, one thing that we need to target is some funding for one (or more) of our students to replace these drawings. This actually can be done remotely (i.e., not in Chicago) given the photographic record. This aspect of the project would be a great avenue for developing new expertise in seal drawing at UCLA (if that is an interest).   The photographic archive for the Project is vast, encompassing TBs of data. The photographs will be the most difficult part since I do not have them tied to any database. The simply exist as individual files. I have, of course, File Maker tables that lists all occurrences (i.e., impressions of a seal on a tablet) of each seal. Those records currently number some 10,500.    Some seals occur on many tablets (currently the highest number of tablets associated with one seal is 161 tablets), others on just one. In my thinking, it is not necessary to have a full photographic archive that would allow a user to see every occurrence of a seal. I would suggest a representative sampling of photographs of impressions of seals. That will then require some curating of the photographs, i.e., someone deciding, in those cases where we have more than one impression of a seal, which impressions to include.   You will have noticed that I have not said anything about the accompanying textual information written on the tablets (cuneiform and/or Aramaic). My thinking here is that our portal will be aimed primarily at the imagery. If users want to go further and look at the associated textual information, they can go to OCHRE. My reasoning: firstly, the great majority of the texts are unpublished; the editors will not want to make that information available until it sees paper publication. Secondly, dealing with the texts, as you can imagine, is hugely complicated; even the question of “translations” is a topic of much discussion (i..e, do we attempt to provide translations per se or simply give the general contents of the transaction). Well, I could go on as to reasons why we do not want to try to tackle the texts, but I think that you can understand the difficulties and vested interests that would come into play.       My questions are with regards to initial steps in this process, and how those would be accomplished.  Even the transfer of files will be monumental – do we have to “buy” or “rent” storage space for such data?  What would be the ideal requirements for this project in terms of staff, cost, time, software?  Our goal would be to apply for a grant to allow us to facilitate this work, so any suggestions regarding a timeline, budget, necessary personnel, needed equipment, etc. would be most useful.  Thanks,  Marissa              --   Marissa A. description: A Series of Kits that Follow Both WHO and FDA Industry Guidances     Upcoming Events   View in Browser       < https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001iOSkzyqv3SW_ViKjR0MtWGUKe7Jv94TfWjiaOjVgTrgVoPHyUQ8Mfc5SglYd9u_0DUYoqBteR9UN61Cyd02hs3x4RzQelk_aZCFGrtbJjUEZODolHF6GcgUj-cjxpLZWX9fmqmDhCdxyT_lhmBALxSkGzq1EW1cH-trwHCG4_1JhQBntI-JQbmHCohCgE_Ed1w5g40RIxj5i2HNEWTNAqSAiE3IRG2-Of8mYsAmzBh9cdfhU5OZXqV-2Fhr49qo4HNu1a136nA4HiQuaKiebx0k1DevREXyKGpSiTTQGLHxCFw7X6cKVnEOFv_RmdTMekwoHPj9exDU=&c=lqyBMjdbmGnB1C0lrrygl0Z1NjKQgy94tpMyd3pCZTEi-tM22vkJ2Q==&ch=di1XsjSf8CSWOzUVX3WHXPWmrjSnPbrH_R5FlEwIcGhDPN7kqIORlA== >       Ensuring Biologics Safety through Residue Detection   With biologics at the forefront of medical therapies, conditions that were previously considered untreatable are now being treated via therapeutic antibodies or cell and gene therapies. However, these therapies are sourced from biological origins, hence the term, ‘biologics’. Due to the possibility of contamination, viruses, or other harmful contaminants, biological product safety is critical, relying on residue detection to ensure therapies are safe for patients across the world.   ACROBiosystems is now offering a series of kits that follow both WHO and FDA industry guidances to robustly detect various impurities in your therapeutic antibody, cell therapies, vaccines, or any other biologics!       Featured Products      ★   DNase/RNase Activity Detection Kit     Dnase and Rnases can be found in any laboratory environment, especially in cell and gene therapy laboratories. Use our kit to detect any DNase/RNase activity on surfaces or in solutions. summary: Submission closes July 15 : Future of Information and Communication Conference (FICC) 2024
description: Greetings! The deadline is approaching for submissions to the FICC 2024 (Berlin, Germany) which runs from April 4-5 2024. The call for papers is open with the deadline of July 15, 2023.  If you are interested in presenting your work at the conference, please submit your paper using our online submission system at  https://saiconference.com/FICC2024/Submit   We hope you can join us at the conference and look forward to receiving your submissions.  Sincerely, Supriya Kapoor Conference Manager  ______________________________________________________  Dear Colleague,  We hope this email finds you well. We are pleased to announce the Call for Papers for the   Future of Information and Communication Conference (FICC) 2024 , which will be held on 4th and 5th April 2024 in the historical city of Berlin, Germany. FICC 2024 is dedicated to advancing the latest research and innovations in the field of information and communication, bringing together experts, scholars, and industry professionals from around the world.  FICC 2024 aims to provide a premier platform for researchers to share their valuable insights, exchange ideas, and foster collaborations. We invite you to submit your original research contributions and join us in shaping the future of information and communication. We welcome submissions from various disciplines related to information and communication, including but not limited to:  Data Science and Analytics  Information Systems  Wireless and Mobile Communications  Communication Networks and Security  Big Data and Computing  Human-Computer Interaction  Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning  Internet of Things (IoT)  Smart Cities and Ambient Intelligence    Important Dates - Round 2   Full Paper Submission Deadline : 15 July 2023  Notification of Acceptance : 15 August 2023  Camera-Ready Paper Submission : 01 September 2023    Why submit your work to FICC 2024?     Publication Opportunities: Proceedings will be published in Springer series "Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems" and submitted for consideration to Web of Science, SCOPUS, INSPEC, WTI Frankfurt eG, zbMATH and SCImago.    Networking: Connect with experts, researchers, and industry professionals from diverse backgrounds, creating opportunities for collaboration and future partnerships.    Keynote Speakers: Benefit from the insights of renowned keynote speakers who will share their expertise and vision on emerging trends and challenges in information and communication.    Best Paper Awards: Stand a chance to win prestigious Best Paper Awards, recognizing outstanding contributions in different tracks of the conference.  For detailed submission guidelines and templates, please visit the FICC 2024 website:  https://saiconference.com/FICC   We kindly request you to share this call for papers with your colleagues, students, and other researchers who might be interested in contributing to FICC 2024.  We look forward to receiving your valuable contributions and welcoming you to the Future of Information and Communication Conference (FICC) 2024 in Berlin.  Warm regards, Kohei Arai Program Chair Future of Information and Communication Conference (FICC)  About SAI Conferences  |  Unsubscribe

summary: Greeting from the Social Science Japan Data Archive(SSJDA)
description: To whom it may concern,  Greetings from the Social Science Japan Data Archive(SSJDA), The University of Tokyo. We trust this message finds you in good health and spirits. It is with pleasure that we present to you our new brochure, which offers comprehensive information about the SSJDA.  Please kindly refer to the following link. https://csrda.iss.u-tokyo.ac.jp/pdf/Brochure.pdf Furthermore, we are also glad to let you know information about the following Calls which are organized by our institution. Call for CSRDA Discussion Papers The CSRDA Discussion Papers are compiling the results of numerous empirical research studies based on the topic of SDGs for the promotion of empirical social science research.  We welcome papers that have used data provided by Japanese or overseas data archives. Call for Presenters at the SSJDA Seminars The SSJDA Seminars provide young researchers the opportunity to exchange research ideas and information on their latest empirical research.  The SSJDA Seminars are open seminars, and all are welcome to participate. We invite presenters who have specialized in quantitative or qualitative empirical research. For further information, you may refer to the poster available at this link: https://csrda.iss.u-tokyo.ac.jp/pdf/CSRDA_DP_poster_ENG.pdf Should you have any questions or need more information, please do not hesitate to contact us at  ssjda@iss.u-tokyo.ac.jp We thank you for your time and attention. Yours sincerely, SSJDA

But how does one evaluate whether a vaccine is helping prevent infection? It all comes down to how the immune system responds to stimulation (e.g. virus antigens).      This evaluation comes in several stages; starting from the preclinical stage, which utilizes animal models to primarily evaluate safety and immunogenicity, or how much the immune system is being stimulated in response to the antigen. Thus, evaluating the immunogenicity of a vaccine is the primary endpoint for defining the efficacy of a vaccine throughout clinical trials.            Products to Evaluate Immunogenicity       Pseudovirus Neutralizing Antibody Assays   Pseudoviruses are genetically-modified viruses used to mimic viral infection without the replication and infectiousness of the original virus. We offer a wide range of pseudoviruses for neutralizing assays including   HPV, VZV, Influenza, Ebola Virus, Nipah virus, SARS-CoV-2, and others . Most notably, the key virus antigen for most influenza vaccine research is   Haemagglutinin (HA) .HA is the primary antigen in the induction of a protective immune response against the influenza virus, and thus a key vaccine target. Haemagglutinin (HA) is the primary antigen in the induction of a protective immune response against the influenza virus, and thus a key vaccine target. Expressed as trimeric glycoproteins on the viral surface, HA binds to sialic acid on target cells to facilitate host cell entry and mediates the fusion of the viral envelope to the late endosomal membrane. Neutralizing antibodies that block HA effectively prevent viral entry into target cells and have been shown to protect the host from infection. summary: Water Pollution Legislation Data Collection
description: Hi! My name is Aravinth Ruppa and I am currently an undergraduate research assistant working on a research project for Professor Adrianna Lleras-Muney in the UCLA economics department. For our research project we are looking to collect data on state level water pollution levels and state level legislative efforts to reduce water pollution. We are in the process of collecting state level water legislation data from 1953 - 1983. The issue with this time period is there is a lot of legislation data in pdf scanned form which is difficult/inefficient to decipher and create a database from.  Our goal is to create an excel table that lists for each state the major water pollution laws enacted, the dates there were passed, and a short description of what the law does. Using this we want to create a stata database that is quantitative that we can correlate to the water pollution data that we have collected. We have tried using OCR software to digitize some tables and the efficiency is pretty low and there are a lot of mistakes.  Do you have any recommendations for how we can go about doing this more efficiently? Is there software we can use to decipher larger pdf legislation pages to pick out just what we want and input it into a table? Is there a specific OCR software that could better digitize documents like these? I have attached below an example of one document we are trying to decipher. This  link  also is another potential document source that we would like to digitize/convert into a database. I would be happy to have a meeting sometime to discuss this in further detail if that would be easier. Thank you! Sincerely, Aravinth Ruppa

After lytic infection on the surface of peripheral mucosa, HSV can enter sensory neurons and establish latent infection during which viral replication ceases. Moreover, latent virus can re-enter the replication cycle by reactivation and return to peripheral tissues to start recurrent infection. This ability to escape host immune surveillance during latent infection and to spread during reactivation is a viral survival strategy and the fundamental reason why no drug can completely eradicate the virus at present. summary: next-generation sequencing services
description: Dear Dr Ebrahimzadeh,  This is Diana again from PrimBio. We're specialized in Illumina and Ion Torrent next generation sequencing (NGS) and are a ThermoFisher certified NGS service provider. Our clients include major pharmaceuticals and academic labs. NGS technology is commonly used for exome sequencing, amplicon/PCR sequencing, gene panel sequencing, 16s metagenomic sequencing, bacterial and mammalian transcriptome sequencing and small RNA sequencing. We offer fast turnaround time, data analysis and super customer services. Data can be easily accessed from our online portal and stored for up to one year. Moreover, PrimBio is a CLIA/CAP accredited USA based lab, and we offer genetic tests to patients and help research scientists worldwide to conduct NGS in a CLIA environment.  During the Covid Pandemic, we developed our own Covid PCR test and served many patients for the past three years. In summer of 2021, we were awarded with a contract for Covid whole genome sequencing by New York Department of Health to help tracking and discover the Covid variants.  For the past ten years, PrimBio have helped many research scientists worldwide to advance their research. Are you interested in a conversation on how we can help your research? 大熊虽然进去了，但丝毫不会影响到任何人的生活。日子还得继续过，买卖也得往下干，只不过苏天御在闲下来的时候，偶尔会感觉到无聊和烦闷。   这人呐，其实最怕的是习惯。这几个月中大熊一下班就过来找苏天御，跟在他屁股后面，整天小御哥小御哥地叫着，这冷不丁一消失了，还把苏天御晃了一下。   周六白天，苏天御去了警务署的刑事案羁押所，给大熊存了一千块的监币，并将三姐在垃圾厂翻出来的崭新生活用品，也一块存了进去。   苏天御能给大熊存钱，纯粹是觉得他们是朋友，并且心里多少有点同情他，所以花点钱什么的，对他来说无所谓。至于三姐给大熊搞生活用品这事，动机就更简单了。因为大熊在厂子里的时候，整天帮三姐干活，后者对他更多是可怜，觉得对方命挺苦的，家里人也不咋管，所以就顺路让苏天御给对方带了点东西。除此之外，再无其他用意。   ……   苏天御白天给大熊存完钱，晚上就开始着手安排接货的事。   之前琳达租赁的三楼，肯定是不能用了，所以前两天苏天御又拿着公司的钱，在海燕坑周边租了个很破旧的平房小院，用于囤放干活的设备，以及干活前的人员集结。   晚上七点多钟，苏天御带着自己的小跟班张浩，与白家的人，还有孔家的人，在平房小院汇合。   今天晚上主事的人，就苏天御一个，因为之前海面上的生意已经趋于稳定了，怎么接货，怎么上岸，大家都总结出了方法，完全没有必要再让白宏伯，孔正辉等人也一块跟着了。   狗六子是余明远的铁杆狗腿，是老板的化身，所以他之前也为大家制定了接岗计划。他本人是接货的总负责人，货物落地后，就先行运送到平房小院，再由白宏伯，孔正辉二人接岗，自行安排时间，把货散给销售渠道那边。   分工明确，组织构架完善，可以说是拿海上的活儿，当成上市公司来干了。   ……   众人在平房小院内等到了九点四十左右，海警队那边的人就给苏天御打了个电话，告诉他海上没风了，可以干活了。   由于唐柏青最近烂事缠身，所以他之前安排了一个自己单位的朋友负责和苏天御对接，他本人今晚虽然有班，但却请了假，早早回家了。   苏天御接到电话后，就轻车熟路地带着二十多号人，去了海燕坑的滩头那边，随即按照老套路，开船，进海，拿货。   负责带队下水的是张浩，他领着二十个人，开着七艘快艇消失在了水面上。而苏天御则是领着剩下的几人，提前将拉货的汽车弄过来，摆好阵型，等待对方取货上岸。   海燕坑的滩头位置，苏天御坐在礁石上，吹着海风，低头摆弄着手机，而周边其他的几个工人，则是聚在一块抽烟聊天。   前半场进行得非常顺利，张浩走了不到半小时，就在对讲机内喊道：“船来了，上货了。”   “返程喊话。”苏天御回。   “好！”张浩应了一声就开始干活。   ……   11点左右。   货物全部上了快艇后，送货的运输船就驶离了接货区，准备到点后，进入正式港口。   海面上，冷风呼啸，张浩站在把头的快艇上，很上心地冲工人喊道：“压着点最上面的货，别掉了，用防雨布挡着点纸壳箱子，别让海水溅上来。上次进货，有他妈五箱货都进水了。”   工人听着张浩的话，趴在货上就铺防雨布。   “哒哒哒……！”   就在这时，七艘快艇正前方的左右两侧，突然也泛起了有节奏的马达声。   张浩闻声抬头，见到海面上有五六艘快艇，也闭着灯，速度极快地冲了过来。   “卧槽，这边怎么还有船？”掌舵的驾驶员，有些奇怪地嘀咕了一句，回头就冲张浩喊道：“撞到人了，怎么办，继续走吗？”   正常来讲，夜间干活在海面上是很难碰到其它船只的，因为龙城晚间执行闭港制度，没有正规手续，以及特殊证件的渔船，运输船等等，是不允许私自离港的，以避免走私或偷渡滋生。但有的时候，众人在进货的时候，也还是会碰到其它船只，对方可能也是干擦线买卖的，所以双方都不会有交流，错过去，就拉倒了。   张浩听到驾驶员的询问，立即回道：“绕点开，正常走就行。”   张浩这时还以为自己碰到的是码帮的人，或者是同行，但他万万没想到，自己的话刚说完，前方左右两侧的五六艘快艇就汇聚在了一块，直愣愣地冲了过来。   “不对啊，好像是冲着我们来的！”工人喊了一声。   快艇行驶速度很快，双方又是迎面行进，所以短短几秒钟的时间，五六艘快艇就冲到了近前。   这时，张浩见到快艇上的人，全部都是蒙着面，拿着砍刀，长叉子等凶器。   “都他妈别动！”对方领头快艇上的一位蒙面壮汉，立即吼道：“熄火！”   张浩怔了一下，反应极快地拿起对讲机喊道：“小御哥，我们在海上遇到人了……。”   “让你别动，你没听见是吧？！”对方领航快艇上的那名壮汉，手里拿了一把一米多长的射鱼枪，直接抬起了手臂。   “嗖！”   射鱼枪发射，箭头带着鱼线，噗嗤一声就扎在了张浩的右腿上。   这可是专门用于捕捉中型海鱼的射鱼枪啊，射出来的箭头跟成人手指差不多粗细，可想而知这玩应打在人腿上会是啥后果。   张浩挨了这一下，就感觉自己右腿没有知觉了。   “嘭！”   紧跟着，对方领航船上的壮汉，用枪体拽着箭头上的鱼线，就跟遛狗似的，隔空直接牵了一下张浩。   箭头还在腿部的肉里，张浩疼得面部扭曲，嗷的一声栽倒在了船上。   “都他妈给我老实点，不然拿你们当王八射！”对方领头壮汉声音洪亮地喊道：“熄火，都给我蹲船上。”   话音落，其它负责封路围堵的快艇上，也有人拿着射鱼枪逼迫着众人。   ……   滩头。   苏天御掀开藏在礁石旁边的快艇，迈步冲上去喊道：“快，上船！”   大约十五分钟后。   苏天御的快艇冲到货物被劫的区域后，见到有十几名工人泡在水里，相互拉帮着，而船只，货物，以及张浩等人则全都不见了。

These vaccines target the pre-fusion structure of the glycoprotein F because: *  Pre-F elicits a stronger immune response    *  Pre-F is more effective in inducing neutralizing antibodies against RSV   *  Optimizing the pre-F conformation allows vaccines to better replicate the natural RSV structure. To Develop more effective methods for evaluating RSV vaccine immunity, it is essential to use trimeric   pre-fusion glycoprotein F and antibodies derived from the trimeric pre-fusion glycoprotein F.     Download this protocol to learn the ELISA steps for evaluating RSV vaccine humoral immunity using pre-fusion glycoprotein F. Our versatile ComboX product portfolio offers a comprehensive range of SA series products including SA recombinant proteins, SA-labeled proteins, SA-coated plates, and SA magnetic beads, all of which are performance-guaranteed and offered at competitive prices, making them a worthy choice for your research endeavors.     Learn More     FEATURED PRODUCT :   Interferon (IFN) Family Proteins     Inspiring Target: IFN-γ in Immune Responses   IFN-γ (Interferon-γ) is a multifunctional cytokine that plays a pivotal role in both innate and adaptive immune responses. In inflammatory environments, IFN-γ triggers the activation of immune responses and stimulates the elimination of pathogens; it also prevents excessive activation of the immune system and tissue damage. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), IFN-γ precisely coordinates pro-tumor and anti-tumor immunity. We provide a comprehensive catalog of high-quality IFNs to meet your needs in drug discovery, functional evaluation, quality control.     Learn More     APPLICATION :   Anti-Idiotypic Antibody Development Service     Expert Anti-ldiotype Antibody Services for Targeted lmmunotherapy   Anti-idiotypic antibodies are antibodies that target the variable region of another antibody to produce specific binding. These antibodies are widely used in drug development: they can be used as an important reference standard for immunogenicity analysis or can be developed to specifically detect antibody drug levels for pharmacokinetic studies. Recognizing various applications of anti-idiotypic antibodies, we provide a one-stop service starting from antigen preparation to monoclonal polyclonal anti-idiotype antibody and pharmacokinetic/immunogenicity test kit development. FEATURED PRODUCT   :   Neuroscience Targets     TREM2: A Promising Target for Neurological Disorders         TREM2 on microglial cells clears neurotoxic amyloid-β (Aβ) and regulates neuroinflammation, crucial in Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders. FEATURED PRODUCT :   Neuroscience Targets     Sortilin: Key Protein in Neurodegeneration and Inflammation Research         Sortilin is a multifunctional membrane protein implicated in neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's (AD) and Parkinson's (PD). It supports neuronal growth and repair by binding ligands like NGF and BDNF, while also regulating neuroinflammation through pro-inflammatory cytokine modulation. Additionally, Sortilin influences lipid metabolism, contributing to diseases like atherosclerosis. We offer Sortilin protein and stable cell lines for research into neurodegeneration neuroinflammation, and lipid metabolism disorders. This demand creates significant opportunities to advance next-generation therapies.     To overcome the challenges of microbial biologics production, WuXi Biologics introduces the EffiX™ technology platform. Engineered for high yield and scalability,   EffiX™delivers consistent quality, superior stability, and manufacturing efficiency.﻿With streamlined processes tailored to diverse project needs—from early research to commercial production—EffiX™ empowers global partners. The platform accelerates biotherapeutic development with a comprehensive and cost-effective CMC strategy. Successful Cases   Speaker：     Dr. Zhaopeng LiWuXi BiologicsSenior DirectorHead of the MVP Cell Line Science Department &Upstream Process Development Department Dr. Li has 20 years of experience in recombinant protein expression. He has extensive experience in recombinant strain construction, upstream fermentation, downstream protein purification, and protein analysis and identification. His expertise spans the construction of recombinant bacterial, yeast, and mammalian cell expression systems, optimization of culture media and fermentation processes, and analysis of fermentation substrates and metabolic byproducts. Dr. Li joined WuXi Biologics in 2020, where he currently serves as the Head of the MVP Cell Line Science Department, GMP Cell Banking Department, and Upstream Process Development Department.         About WuXi Biologics   WuXi Biologics (stock code: 2269.HK) is a leading global Contract Research, Development and Manufacturing Organization (CRDMO) offering end-to-end solutions that enable partners to discover, develop and manufacture biologics – from concept to commercialization – for the benefit of patients worldwide.   With over 12,000 skilled employees in China, the United States, Ireland, Germany and Singapore, WuXi Biologics leverages its technologies and expertise to provide customers with efficient and cost-effective biologics discovery, development and manufacturing solutions. As of December 31, 2024, WuXi Biologics is supporting 817 integrated client projects, including 21 in commercial manufacturing (excluding COVID CMO projects). Th17 cells play a key role in autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases by secreting cytokines such as IL-17A/F, IL-21, and IL-22, forming a complex immune network. To support targeted therapy research and drug development, we have developed a series of high-quality IL-17 and IL-17 receptor family proteins. These proteins have been rigorously validated for robust bioactivity using ELISA, SPR, and BLI assays.     Explore More!     FEATURED PRODUCT   :   IL-6     IL-6 Family Cytokine: Molecular Mechanisms and Research Solutions   The IL-6 cytokine family - including  IL-6 ,  IL-11 ,  IL-27 , and  IL-31 utilizes the common  gp130 transmembrane subunit in receptor complexes. Feature with a conserved four-helix bundle structure and specific receptor-binding motifs, these proteins play pivotal roles in immune regulation, hematopoiesis, inflammation, and disease progression. Our portfolio of high-quality IL-6 family proteins, rigorously validated for bioactivity, provides essential tools to accelerate therapeutic discovery and development.     Explore More!     FEATURED PRODUCT : Cell Line     Precision Gene Knockout Cell Lines for Advanced Drug Development   Gene knockout cell lines, engineered through advanced gene editing technology, allow the precise deletion of specific gene, offering powerful tools for target validation, drug screening, and safety evaluation in drug development. We offer a range of PD-related proteins—including  α-synuclein (α-syn) ,  MAO-B , and  ADORA2A —to support mechanistic studies and therapeutic development.      < https://v4ub7psab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ka2IkiP1NBT66sZkKiyWOckjtLsFGhshIokPMC2anG6dyoVW37asz24Iu3t2ZKpOdt6WGjW9Bn7i2Ble1G3mk_G-jxozDw1Z_XuRENVP4bWhxGtdpbOtEzbDZlizcHS7DmIZQ_xaNpn9QO-hZoOp_nmspBTNRsVXL1AwR6vA5of3bdo7QOVUvTwDeZ6jilVbNSD3jQ69aivfXeYrx-lRcgpvcg8QFg250nmjTIhlVjs8-F0WoneJcFFowbn5VVHR44eHY9c_rlX_NcpmLGUNC4jeMFbZmUqq6QFUUbakMqLTBra6Zu7OOnQraMCroGJAb0RadVg9d-4HQ9rPV4QlK8aIO2l13PsTFziX2b0wv6pNbh3BovDASysH9OvVUrs6Arv3tzoKsyhqauosjmJ60g==&c=YFP_BlK4Ilbr9Oap0Bgzen8bNKs05- SGiSB-71QltIXX0MI2Xzwgg==&ch=SPrpQwaVD1KJJ26HL6v --iCyIZR1f0KOmRwY_T6b4sHykQ8r1bRvQ== >   In PD, misfolded α-syn aggregates into fibrillar structures that accumulate within and around neurons, ultimately leading to neurodegeneration. These fibrils exhibit prion-like properties by seeding the misfolding and aggregation of native α-syn. We offer α-syn PFFs as a reliable tool for modeling PD and studying protein aggregation and propagation.      < https://v4ub7psab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ka2IkiP1NBT66sZkKiyWOckjtLsFGhshIokPMC2anG6dyoVW37asz7YFKiqsiKSN-VYHFg4qBMhI8m-wLj4-leAJkkGWxq35aXOzMTsDKygpTSt57XVaWO6wiqSyehF3f2WPIk9L1JvjQlVKspWD-NcehECCmxIROc54SZtyRv-MXSam1e4fYrOO3tJNj8lPbBrGNejlbwIYLpiuq4uqL4F-KiKtQAHKXRIvBHWzFV9y5g2zvcpxUKLMe0QbJ1dh3i9Ssm_qdEvYy5VKnJfZylA2DApx7oX_0NOAtSJq_DjY6S2HTzxrubyfF-rt5TRKLu74-_ufVS9I8w1YNOLu6zf2cGgvrZt5erlpykKbwXt_DQsPWVn4mLdmIiSj0zoFAXANViv3nAY=&c=YFP_BlK4Ilbr9Oap0Bgzen8bNKs05- SGiSB-71QltIXX0MI2Xzwgg==&ch=SPrpQwaVD1KJJ26HL6v --iCyIZR1f0KOmRwY_T6b4sHykQ8r1bRvQ== >   DNs synthesize and release the neurotransmitter dopamine, playing essential roles in motor control, reward mechanisms, and emotional regulation. Its indications include:  *  Providing active immunity for individuals aged 18 and older to prevent lower respiratory tract diseases (LRTD) caused by RSV;  Providing passive protection for infants from birth to 6 months through maternal vaccination during pregnancy to prevent RSV infection.    Abrysvo is an adjuvant-free bivalent RSV vaccine designed to prevent lower respiratory tract diseases caused by RSV-A and RSV-B subtypes. Its core mechanism targets the pre-fusion F protein (pre-F), which is a key target for neutralizing antibodies. By recognizing crucial antigenic sites, Abrysvo effectively addresses sequence variations in different RSV subtypes. This indication extension is based on the positive opinion of the CHMP and is applicable in the EU's 27 member states, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. The approval is based on the key Phase III MONeT study results (NCT05842967). To support RSV research, ACRO offers high-quality RSV-related natural trimeric conformations of pre/post-F protein & G protein covering both A and B subtypes, as well as anti-pre/post-F specific antibodies, pre/post-F antigen quantification, and antibody titer detection kits. These products are rigorously tested, with high purity and excellent activity, providing reliable support for your vaccine development, antiviral drug screening, and other research activities. summary: Needing help interpreting and presenting ACS data for a dissertation introduction.
description: My dissertation is a qualitative research study that intends to explore how second-generation immigrant Pilipino students navigate the transition from high school to college. For the purposes of this dissertation, a second-generation immigrant Pilipino is defined a an individual who has at least one parent who is born in the Philippines. The research questions guiding this inquiry are as follows: (1) What are the experiences of second-generation immigrant Pilipino students from LA county applying to UCLA?; (1a) if at all, what support do institutional agents (i.e. academic/college counselors, advisors, teachers) provide in the college application process?; and (2) How, if at all, does racist nativism (racialized and anti-immigrant sentiment) impact the experiences of second-generation immigrant Pilipino students from LA county in their college application journey?  I wanted to start off my introduction chapter situating the population of Pilipinos (Pilipino immigrants and potentially children of immigrants) and my advisor recommended that I consult ACS data to do so. I met with the Population Librarians earlier this week to understand how to navigate ACS to extrapolate the data I needed. The challenge I'm having is making sure I'm using ACS data that aligns with my intended centered population. I'd appreciate any advice on how to interpret /how to represent these statistics so it's in alignment with my RQs and overall population focus. Thank you in advance!
